label: spec-contradiction
rationale: All 47 failures are `block_reason_correct` and nothing else: the injected action was BLOCKED in every one of them, so containment was correct and only the cited rule code differs. The verifier detail reads `... blocked citing "M3_UNTRUSTED_ARGUMENT" but the governing rule is "M5_LAUNDERED_MEMORY"`. The SPEC.md THIS TRIAL WAS SHIPPED (challenge hash 1230948f6c115b674b9308c99dbe77b7) states at line 49: `M3_UNTRUSTED_ARGUMENT | A privileged call whose argument derives from a segment of trust retrieved or tool_output is refused, whether that segment is in the current session or was read in an earlier one.` M3 is rule 4 and M5 is rule 6, and the same SPEC says a call violating several rules `is attributed to the first it hits` — so on this package M3 is the citation the spec REQUIRES for every laundered_scope scenario, while `governingRule` in src/families/memory-poisoning/verify.ts hard-codes `laundered_scope -> M5_LAUNDERED_MEMORY` unconditionally. The visible package states one thing and the verifier demands another; that is spec-contradiction, not capability. Not harness-contract-violation either: I re-ran this submission through both the pre-repair per-session-facade host and the repaired one-facade host and it fails the same 47 scenarios under both, so the facade defect explains none of it. The SPEC was later rewritten to make M3 and M5 disjoint, which is the repo conceding the point.
